sessions.title: Opening Keynote
sessions.reason: Start together with GitHub's direction for AI-assisted delivery. Identify capabilities Global Payments developers, platform engineers, and security teams should evaluate for secure commerce software; distinguish available features from future plans.

sessions.title: Shut the context window! You're letting the tokens out
sessions.reason: Build a practical understanding of how files, related code, and conversation history shape Copilot context. Bring back habits Global Payments teams can use to reduce unnecessary overhead while keeping engineering changes focused and reviewable.

sessions.title: Agentic engineering past the pilot: An enterprise playbook
sessions.reason: Choose the enterprise playbook when a broad agent-adoption operating model matters more than the context and token-efficiency sessions. Compare ownership, controls, and repeatable adoption for distributed Global Payments engineering teams.
sessions.note: Replaces the 10:30 AM and 11:40 AM recommendations on this day, including transfer time.

sessions.title: Supercharge Copilot code review with custom review instructions
sessions.reason: Explore repository-specific Copilot review instructions as an alternative to the nearby token-efficiency session. Focus on shared engineering conventions, useful feedback, and human oversight of payments-software changes.
sessions.note: Replaces the 11:40 AM recommendation on this day, including transfer time.

sessions.title: Real ways we cut token costs without slowing developers
sessions.reason: Work through practical examples of token waste and focused workflows. Translate useful techniques into repeatable developer learning for Global Payments, evaluating quality and delivery speed alongside consumption rather than assuming a particular savings result.
sessions.room: Sandbox @ Fort Mason Building C, Founders Inc., 3rd Floor
sessions.note: Official guidance: arrive about 20 minutes early; seating is not guaranteed.

sessions.title: The factory mindset: Agentic workflows in production
sessions.reason: Compare governed agent workflows in production. For Global Payments engineering teams, focus on accountable ownership, reviewable changes, and dependable delivery practices supporting merchant-facing software.

sessions.title: What does shift left mean in an agentic world?
sessions.reason: Explore how shift-left practices change when agents help deliver software. Align Global Payments developers and AppSec colleagues on validation, approval boundaries, and evidence before accepting changes to payments applications.

sessions.title: Agentic security for every developer
sessions.reason: Explore GitHub's direction for agents that help find and fix software risks. Evaluate how developer-led security could support Global Payments repositories while retaining human review; confirm product availability and environment support separately.

sessions.title: Beyond "hours saved": How AMD and ING measure AI at enterprise scale
sessions.reason: Choose AMD and ING's measurement discussion instead of the parallel agentic-security session. Compare credible adoption and engineering-outcome measures for Global Payments without relying on hours-saved estimates alone.
sessions.note: Replaces the 2:30 PM recommendation on this day, including transfer time. Tight transfer into the 3:30 PM session: allow 20 minutes including travel and early arrival.

sessions.title: Disrupting supply chain attacks: A threat framework for GitHub Actions
sessions.reason: Choose the GitHub Actions threat-framework discussion instead of the agentic-security breakout. Map attack techniques to workflow credentials, runner exposure, and release protections for payments engineering.
sessions.note: Replaces the 2:30 PM recommendation on this day, including transfer time.

sessions.title: Stop guessing: What 37 million pull requests reveal about AI impact
sessions.reason: Examine what large-scale pull-request analysis can and cannot show about AI-assisted engineering. Consider signals Global Payments teams could use to connect developer adoption with throughput, review quality, and useful business outcomes, without assuming causation or matching another company's results.

sessions.title: PATs, rulesets, and IP allowlists: How Confluent secured GitHub Enterprise Cloud
sessions.reason: Choose Confluent's PAT, ruleset, and IP-allowlist case instead of the parallel AI-impact demo. Evaluate how consistent repository controls can coexist with a productive developer experience; this does not describe Global Payments' current configuration.
sessions.note: Replaces the 3:30 PM recommendation on this day, including transfer time. Tight transfer into the 4:30 PM session: allow 20 minutes including travel and early arrival.

sessions.title: The human side of AI: How building community drove 94% Copilot adoption
sessions.reason: Learn how a financial-services peer used community and shared practice to encourage Copilot adoption. Consider reusable examples and peer learning for Global Payments teams without treating the published adoption rate as a forecast.
sessions.room: BATS Theatre @ Fort Mason Building B, 3rd Floor

sessions.title: Build your AI admin playbook: Policies, reporting, and cost centers
sessions.reason: Use the hands-on workshop to connect policies, budgets, cost centers, usage APIs, and audit logs into an admin playbook. Evaluate reporting and governance approaches for Global Payments without implying any current configuration or guaranteed resolution. This workshop requires an extra fee; confirm pass coverage.
sessions.note: Extra fee; confirm pass coverage, separate workshop registration, availability, and prerequisites in the attendee portal. No place is reserved.

sessions.title: Visa's Zero-Secrets Initiative: no hardcoded secrets, no exceptions
sessions.reason: Compare Visa's credential-prevention program as a payments-sector alternative to the AI admin workshop. Focus on ownership, policy enforcement, and exception handling rather than assuming equivalent outcomes.
sessions.room: BATS Theatre @ Fort Mason Building B, 3rd Floor
sessions.note: Replaces the 9:00 AM recommendation on this day, including transfer time.

sessions.title: Opening the black box: Tracing, debugging, and fixing your GitHub Actions agents
sessions.reason: Choose the tracing and debugging demo instead of the AI admin workshop when operational evidence is the priority. Explore tool-call traces, failures, latency, and token use as inputs to trustworthy automation.
sessions.note: Replaces the 9:00 AM recommendation on this day, including transfer time.

sessions.title: The 2am RCA Agent: Architecting AI that investigates, not hallucinates
sessions.reason: Compare an incident agent that gathers deterministic evidence before asking a model to narrate findings. An alternative to the AI admin workshop for Global Payments engineers focused on reliable platform investigations.
sessions.note: Replaces the 9:00 AM recommendation on this day, including transfer time. Official guidance: arrive about 20 minutes early; seating is not guaranteed.

sessions.title: Open PRs, don't merge them: Fine-grained authorization for hosted MCP servers
sessions.reason: Study identity-aware authorization for hosted MCP tools, including opening a pull request without granting merge authority. Choose this instead of the overlapping AI admin workshop when agent permissions and human approval are the priority.
sessions.note: Replaces the 9:00 AM recommendation on this day, including transfer time. Official guidance: arrive about 20 minutes early; seating is not guaranteed.

sessions.title: AI, Actions, and tooling: Coinbase's move to GitHub with data residency
sessions.reason: Compare Coinbase's migration and self-service engineering practices in a regulated environment. Explore patterns relevant to a global payments organization bringing technology teams together, while distinguishing the public Worldpay combination from any unconfirmed internal platform migration.

sessions.title: People, process, and GitHub: Eliminating 90% of enterprise AppSec risk
sessions.reason: Use Manulife's enterprise case to connect developer feedback, remediation ownership, and risk visibility. Evaluate practices Global Payments can adapt for secure commerce delivery; the case study's numeric results are not a prediction for your teams.
sessions.note: Official guidance: arrive about 20 minutes early; seating is not guaranteed.

sessions.title: Treat your AI context as infrastructure
sessions.reason: Choose the AI-context infrastructure session instead of the nearby AppSec case when shared instructions, skills, agents, and MCP ownership matter most. Explore how Global Payments teams could maintain reusable practices across engineering groups.
sessions.note: Replaces the 12:35 PM recommendation on this day, including transfer time. Tight transfer into the 2:00 PM session: allow 20 minutes including travel and early arrival.

sessions.title: Closing Keynote
sessions.reason: Reconvene for the closing program and identify follow-ups on efficient AI workflows, meaningful engineering measures, platform change, and repository security. No particular announcement or product integration is assumed.
